questions.q_en:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. She is the best dancer in the competition. She is a talented performer.

B. She is a best dancer in the competition. She is a talented performer.

C. She is the best dancer in competition. She is a talented performer.

D. She is the best dancer in competition. She is an talented performer.
questions.solution_en:
A: Correct

"The best dancer" is correct because "best" is a superlative adjective. A superlative adjective shall be followed by the definite article "the". And "a talented performer" is correct because "talented" starts with a consonant sound and aptly follows the indefinite article "a". This is because "a" is used before consonant-sounding words.

B: Incorrect

"A best dancer" is incorrect because "best" is a superlative, and superlatives should be used with "the." "A talented performer" is correct.

C: Incorrect

"The best dancer" is correct, but "in competition" should be "in the competition" to specify a particular competition. "A talented performer" is correct.

D: Incorrect

"In competition" should be "in the competition" to specify a particular competition. "An talented" is incorrect as "talented" starts with a consonant sound and requires the indefinite article "a" before it. This is because "an" is used before vowel-sounding words.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

Large glasses magnified his eyes so that to gave him the appearance of a wise owl.
questions.solution_en:
The infinitive marker 'to' should be followed by the base verb, whereas 'gave' is the past simple (V2) form of verb. So, the underlined segment requires substitution.

Option (b) repeats the same error, hence it is negated.

'It' in option (c) is singular pronoun which cannot be used to refer to the plural noun 'glasses'. So, option (c) is negated as well.

'So as to' means the same as 'in order to'. Replacing the underlined segment with it makes the sentence contextually and grammatically correct.

The correct sentence is: Large glasses magnified his eyes so as to give him the appearance of a wise owl.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The national anthem was being sung very enthusiastically by young students in the annual event.
options_en: The young students in the annual event were singing the national anthem very enthusiastically.
The national anthem was sung very enthusiastically for young students in the annual event.
The young students in the annual event had been singing the national anthem very enthusiastically.
The national anthem sang the young students very enthusiastically.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The young students in the annual event were singing the national anthem very enthusiastically.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Teena said, "I painted all the pots in my garden."
options_en: Teena said that she had been painted all the pots in her garden.
Teena said that she have painted all the pots in her garden.
Teena told that she had being painted all the pots in her garden.
Teena said that she had painted all the pots in her garden.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'she'.

· The verb 'painted' (past simple) is changed into 'had painted' (past perfect).

· Possessive determiner 'my' changed to 'her'.

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

None of the options except (d) follows these changes. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Teena said that she had painted all the pots in her garden.

Note:-

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

In recent times, the Indian IPO market has experienced significant growth, driven by various Government of India (GOI) initiatives such as Make in India and Digital India, along with favourable regulations implemented by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). High foreign investment inflows and growing Private Equity (PE) and Venture Capital (VC) exits through IPOs, rather than the traditional mode of exits by selling stakes to other PE funds or through trade sales, have also contributed to this growth. As a result, many tech-led, Indian-founded but overseas-based startups are reverse-flipping to take advantage of the growing interest of both Indian and global investors in the Indian capital markets. Companies like PhonePe and Groww recently moved their headquarters to India, while others like Pine Labs and Flipkart are reportedly exploring similar options.

This shift reflects a more discerning approach, influenced by tight monetary conditions, high inflation, market volatility, global economic slowdown, and increasing regulatory scrutiny. This focus on profitability has enhanced the IPO-readiness of startups, as public market investors typically seek more mature companies with proven revenue models and a clear path to operational profitability.

What trend has been observed among Indian-founded but overseas-based startups in relation to the Indian IPO market?

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop, / admired a few vintage items on display, / and then sits near the ornate fireplace to read his book.
options_en: admired a few vintage items on display,
and then sits near the ornate fireplace to read his book
He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop,
questions.solution_en:
The error is in part (c) regarding verb tense consistency. The sentence describes a sequence of actions in the past: "walked" (V2) and "admired" (V2). To maintain tense consistency, the third verb "sits" (V5 - simple present) should also be in the simple past tense, which is "sat" (V2).

Correct Sentence: He quietly walked into the bustling antique shop, admired a few vintage items on display, and then sat near the ornate fireplace to read his book.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Tense Consistency: In a sentence or paragraph, verbs should generally remain in the same tense unless there's a logical reason for a shift (e.g., describing events at different times).

· V2 (Past form of verb): The form of the verb used to indicate an action that happened in the past.

· V5 (Third person singular): The base form of the verb with -s or -es added, used for third-person singular subjects in the simple present tense.

The conversation which Caesar held ____ (A) Cleopatra deepened the impression which her first appearance had made upon him. Her _____ (B) and animation, the originality of her ideas, and the point and pertinency of her mode of expressing them, made her, independently of her personal charms, an exceedingly entertaining and agreeable companion. She, in fact, _______ (C) won the great conqueror's heart; and, through the strong attachment to her that he immediately formed, he became wholly disqualified to act impartially between her and her brother in regard to their respective _______ (D) to the crown. We call Ptolemy Cleopatra's brother; for, though he was also, in fact, her husband, still, as he was only ten or twelve years of age at the time of Cleopatra's expulsion from Alexandria, the marriage had been probably regarded, thus far, only as a mere matter of form. Caesar was now about fifty-two. He had a wife, named Calpurnia, to ______ (E) he had been married about ten years.

Which of the following words can fill in the blank E?
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a relative pronoun in the objective form to denote Calpurnia, the wife of Caesar. Among the options, 'whom' is the only relative pronoun in the objective form and thus it can fill in the given blank. 'Which' denotes an object and not a person, 'who' is a subjective relative pronoun and 'whose' shows belongingness, so these are negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) along the winding river,

(b) their leaves whispering secrets to the breeze,

(c) ancient trees with gnarled branches stood sentinel,

(d) creating a timeless scene

(e) of tranquil beauty
questions.solution_en:
(a) Along the winding river, - This prepositional phrase sets the location or scene for the sentence. It's a common way to begin a descriptive sentence.

(c) ancient trees with gnarled branches stood sentinel, - This is the main clause of the sentence, introducing the subject ("ancient trees") and the verb ("stood sentinel"). It describes what was present in the scene set by (a). So far: "Along the winding river, ancient trees with gnarled branches stood sentinel,"

(b) their leaves whispering secrets to the breeze, - This absolute phrase provides additional descriptive detail about the "ancient trees," adding to the imagery. It modifies the subject of the main clause. Now: "...stood sentinel, their leaves whispering secrets to the breeze,"

(d) creating a timeless scene - This participial phrase describes the overall effect or result of the elements mentioned so far (the river, the trees, their leaves). It links back to the entire preceding description. "...their leaves whispering secrets to the breeze, creating a timeless scene"

(e) of tranquil beauty - This prepositional phrase completes the description introduced in (d), specifying the nature of the "timeless scene."

Final sentence: "Along the winding river, ancient trees with gnarled branches stood sentinel, their leaves whispering secrets to the breeze, creating a timeless scene of tranquil beauty."

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.solution_en:
The changes that happen while converting Passive voice to Active voice sentence are: the Subject in the Passive voice becomes the Object in the Active voice and the Object in the Passive voice will become the Subject in the Active voice.

The helping verb should be removed while changing from Passive voice to Active voice.

The given Passive voice sentence is in Present Continuous Tense and the Active Voice form will also have the same Present Continuous tense form.

For example:

What is being sold at the counter? (Passive voice)

What is the counter selling? (Active voice)

From the given options, the one that follows the above mentioned changes is option (a), "What is the training institute instructing?"

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

questions.solution_en:

By: This preposition is not suitable in this context. "By" typically indicates a deadline or a point in time, and it does not convey the intended meaning of practising for a purpose.

Between: This preposition is not appropriate here. "Between" is used to express a relationship in terms of time or space involving two or more points. It doesn't convey the idea of practising for a specific purpose.

Under: This preposition is not suitable in this context. "Under" is often used to indicate control, supervision, or influence, and it doesn't convey the intended meaning of practising for a purpose.

The correct sentence is: She practised diligently for hours to prepare for the challenging piano recital next week.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed segment in the given sentence.

The team captain had to (put down) the match due to the sudden unavailability of several key players.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence suggests that the team captain had to postpone or reschedule the match because several important players were unexpectedly unavailable. The original sentence contains an error due to the use of the phrase "put down." The expression "put down" typically means to physically place something on a surface or to euthanize an animal, but it does not convey the intended meaning of postponing or cancelling an event, such as a match in this context.

Option (a) is correct. The phrasal verb "put off" means to postpone or delay something to a later time. In the context of the sentence, it accurately conveys the idea that the team captain had to postpone or reschedule the match due to the sudden unavailability of several key players.

Option (b) is not correct. This phrasal verb "put on" commonly means to dress oneself by placing clothing, accessories, or items onto one's body. However, in the context of the sentence, it doesn't convey the idea of postponement or cancellation of the match due to the unavailability of players.

Option (c) is incorrect. The phrase 'call back' usually means to return a phone call or ask someone to return to a place or situation. However, it doesn't accurately convey the action needed in the given context, where the team captain must take a decision regarding the match due to the absence of key players.

Option (d) is incorrect as well. "Call on" often means to ask for assistance or support from someone. However, in the context of the sentence, it doesn't convey the team captain's action of postponing or cancelling the match due to the sudden unavailability of players.

The correct sentence is: The team captain had to put off the match due to the sudden unavailability of several key players.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The tourist said that he had been searching for that area for a long time.
options_en: The tourist said, "I have been searching for this area for a long time."
The tourist said, "I will be searching for this area for a long time."
The tourist said, "I were searching for this area for a long time."
The tourist said, "I am searching for this area for a long time."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + Present Participle + Object) will be converted into Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have been + Present participle + Object).

For example:

He said that they had been waiting for hours. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "We have been waiting for hours" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
said thatsaid
He had been searchingI have been searching
ThatThis

Of the given options, one that follows the above-mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (a) "The tourist said, "I have been searching for this area for a long time.""

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
